chunks: Sahl, from Ali ibn Hassan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Abu Al-Hasan the First (peace be upon him), who said:
He said: The striking of a man's hand upon his thigh during bereavement leads to the nullification of his reward.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of striking the thigh during grief in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith distinguishes between permissible grief and excessive, uncontrolled mourning (khuruj an al-hudud), identifying the specific gesture of striking the thigh as a sign of impatience that diminishes the reward of sabr. Scholars note that while this act does not necessarily invalidate the prayer or constitute a major sin, it reflects a lack of spiritual composure and thus reduces the merit of the patience shown. This ruling is frequently cited in discussions on the etiquette of mourning, particularly in contrast to the more severe penalty of striking the face or chest.

en.hubeali:
Sahl, from Ali Bin Hassan, from Musa Bin Bakr, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1<sup>st</sup> having said:
‘The man’s striking of his hand upon his thigh during the difficulty (bereavement) leads to confiscation of his Recompense’.
en.sarwar: 9. Sahl has narrated from Ali ibn Hassa’n from Musa ibn Bakr who has said the following: “Abu al-Hassan the 1st, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
A man’s striking his hand on his thigh, when suffering a misfortune, causes suspension of his rewards for his suffering.’”
